newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico reserves, assets rise.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico reserves, assets rise.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said Tuesday its net international assets as of October 25, 1996, were $3.872 billion, compared with $3.745 billion on October 18.
The central bank said that its net international reserves as of October 25 were $15.763 billion, compared with $15.739 billion as of October 18.
It said the increase in international assets was due to:
- Revenues from operations with state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) of $139 million
- Other foreign exchange revenues worth a net $14 million.

- A net loss of $26 million for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates for trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts of commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said the monetary base fell 1.777 billion pesos due to seasonal demand for notes and coins stemming from salary payments for the period from October 18 to 25.
Central bank credit to banks rose 3.383 billion pesos to meet the rising demand for notes and coins.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's assets and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six month duration from other central banks.
